record.paper_title: Zero Sum Trees: A Survey of Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Zero-sum spanning tree conjecture for Z_m-colored complete graphs.
record.original_question: Let m be a positive integer, and let c be an edge-coloring of the complete graph K_{m+1} by elements of the cyclic group Z_m. Must there always exist a spanning tree T of K_{m+1} whose m edges e_1, e_2, ..., e_m have total color sum 0 in Z_m, that is, for which c(e_1) + c(e_2) + ... + c(e_m) = 0 in Z_m?

evidence.quote: Conjecture. In every Zₘ-coloring c of the edges of Kₘ₊₁, the complete graph on m + 1 vertices, there exists a spanning tree of Kₘ₊₁, say T, with edges e₁, e₂, . . . , eₘ satisfying ∑ᵢ₌₁ᵐ c(eᵢ) = 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let m be a positive integer and let K_{m+1} denote the complete graph on m+1 vertices. Let Z_m = Z/mZ denote the cyclic group of order m, and let c : E(K_{m+1}) → Z_m be an arbitrary edge-coloring of K_{m+1} by elements of Z_m. Prove or disprove: there always exists a spanning tree T of K_{m+1}, with edge set {e_1, e_2, …, e_m}, such that
    c(e_1) + c(e_2) + ⋯ + c(e_m) ≡ 0  (mod m).
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture was proved by Z. Füredi and D. Kleitman: for any Z_m-edge-coloring (equivalently, integer weights mod m) of K_{m+1}, there exists a spanning tree whose edge-sum is 0 mod m. A simpler proof and a generalization were later given by Schrijver and Seymour. The result is now a standard theorem in zero-sum Ramsey theory.

status_evidence.title: A simpler proof and a generalization of the zero-trees theorem
status_evidence.snippet: A simpler proof and a generalization of the zero-trees theorem (Schrijver, Seymour).
status_evidence.claim: The zero-sum spanning tree theorem (originally due to Füredi and Kleitman) has been proved and generalized.

status_evidence.title: On Zero-Sum Spanning Trees and Zero-Sum Connectivity
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses zero-sum spanning trees, citing the Füredi–Kleitman theorem as established.
status_evidence.claim: The Z_m zero-sum spanning tree result on K_{m+1} is an established theorem.
